title: Shadow traffic policy: config validation scenarios + edge cases (v1)
body:
Purpose
- Capture validation scenarios + edge cases for Shadow Traffic Policy (control plane) and its interaction with routing/rollouts.
- Intended to become automated tests in the policy-service + integration tests in routing.
- This doc is intentionally “test-case-y” and repetitive; we expect to translate each case into a table-driven suite.

Scope
- Shadow policy config attached to routes and/or rollout variants.
- Validation at:
  (1) API request validation (Console backend -> policy service)
  (2) persistence validation (schema constraints / migrations)
  (3) runtime guardrails (routing fails open, timeouts, circuit breakers)

Non-goals (for this doc)
- Scoring rubric correctness (owned by Applied ML / eval-harness).
- Deep telemetry schema validation (owned by Telemetry; we just reference required fields/dimensions).

Terminology (aligned with ADRs)
- control: the user-visible path/variant response.
- shadow target: candidate variant(s) that receive mirrored requests asynchronously/inline (implementation is “inline mirror + strict timeouts” with fail-open).
- shadow experiment: logical grouping for analysis; may be created explicitly via Console or implicitly via rollout attachment.
- route: routing object that selects model + config (region, fallback policy, etc.).
- deployment mode: Hosted / Dedicated / Private.

Assumptions / constraints baked into validation
- Must be fail-open: user response must not be delayed by shadow path failures.
- Shadow overhead budgets must be enforced (timeouts, max concurrent mirrors, sampling).
- Cardinality guardrails: no high-cardinality fields in tags/labels; prompt_id/customer_id not allowed as metric dimensions.
- Deterministic bucketing: stable across retries within the same route+policy version.

Canonical objects referenced in cases
- shadow_policy:
  - enabled: bool
  - sampling_rate: float (0..1)
  - targets: list[shadow_target] (1..N; N max TBD; propose 4)
  - bucketing: { fingerprint_salt_ref, key_fields, method } (method fixed for v1)
  - headers: allowlist/denylist behavior
  - timeouts: { connect_ms, total_ms } with hard max
  - fail_open: true (forced)
  - shadow_request_budget: { max_parallel, max_qps_per_route?, max_bytes? }
  - streaming_behavior: { mirror_mode, capture_limit_tokens, stop_conditions }
  - data_handling: { redact_profile_id, retention_profile_id }

Validation error conventions (proposal)
- Return HTTP 400 with error_code + field_path + human_message.
- Prefer stable error codes for automation:
  - SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID
  - SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED
  - SHADOW_POLICY_CONFLICT
  - SHADOW_POLICY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
  - SHADOW_POLICY_RBAC_DENIED
  - SHADOW_POLICY_DEPENDENCY_MISSING


SECTION A — Basic schema validation

A1. enabled=false but shadow fields present
- Input: enabled=false, sampling_rate=0.1, targets=[…]
- Expectation: Accept (lenient) OR Reject (strict). Decision needed.
- Recommendation: Accept but ignore all shadow behavior. Log warning (not error).
- Test asserts: stored config preserves fields; runtime ignores.

A2. sampling_rate missing
- Input: enabled=true, targets present, sampling_rate unset
- Expectation: Reject with SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID at shadow_policy.sampling_rate

A3. sampling_rate < 0
- Input: sampling_rate=-0.01
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID; message “sampling_rate must be between 0 and 1”.

A4. sampling_rate > 1
- Input: sampling_rate=1.001
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID.

A5. sampling_rate = 0
- Expectation: Accept; runtime should not mirror; should still emit “policy enabled but no sampling” metric? (optional)
- Note: Console should warn but allow.

A6. sampling_rate = 1
- Expectation: Accept only if budgets allow; runtime will mirror all requests (still fail-open).
- Guardrail: require explicit override flag for 100% in Dedicated/Hosted? (open question)

A7. targets empty
- Input: enabled=true, targets=[]
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID at shadow_policy.targets

A8. targets count exceeds max
- Input: targets=[t1..t10]
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
- Limit suggestion: max 4 targets (v1).

A9. target missing required identifier
- Input: target has neither model_ref nor variant_ref
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID at shadow_policy.targets[i].(model_ref|variant_ref)

A10. duplicate targets
- Input: same target repeated (same model_ref + same config)
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_CONFLICT OR auto-dedupe.
- Recommendation: Reject (prevents accidental cost). Include which indices collide.

A11. target references control variant
- Input: shadow target equals control (same pinned model version + quant profile + prompt template)
- Expectation: Reject or warn.
- Recommendation: Allow but warn; useful to validate pipeline overhead without quality delta.

A12. unknown fields / forward-compat
- Input: shadow_policy.foo_new_field present
- Expectation: Reject (strict) for control plane API; Accept if stored via “passthrough” (not recommended).
- Recommendation: Reject unknown fields for v1.


SECTION B — Route + rollout attachment semantics

B1. Policy attached to route without rollout
- Input: route.shadow_policy enabled
- Expectation: Valid; experiment created implicitly (shadow_experiment_id generated).
- Validation: requires route has stable route_id (no ephemeral routes).

B2. Policy attached to rollout variant
- Input: rollout has control variant + candidate variant; shadow policy says “mirror to candidate variant ref”
- Expectation: Valid; variant_ref must exist in same rollout object.
- Reject if variant_ref not found: SHADOW_POLICY_DEPENDENCY_MISSING.

B3. Both route shadow policy and rollout shadow policy present
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_CONFLICT (ambiguous).
- Alternative: define precedence (rollout overrides route). Needs decision.
- Recommendation: Reject for v1.

B4. Route uses fallback policy + shadow policy also specifies fallback
- Input: route fallback: region_failover; shadow target fallback: different
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_CONFLICT OR normalize.
- Recommendation: Shadow target inherits fallback behavior from target’s route/variant only; prohibit “shadow-specific fallback knobs” in v1.

B5. Policy attached to route with “pin model version” absent
- Input: route uses floating “latest” model
- Expectation: Allow, but note that comparing control vs shadow will drift.
- Recommendation: Allow with Console warning; optionally require explicit pin for “quality gates”.

B6. Updating a shadow policy mid-experiment
- Input: same route_id; update targets or sampling_rate
- Expectation: Allowed, but results should segment by policy_revision_id.
- Validation: require last_modified_by + audit log entry.


SECTION C — Deterministic bucketing / fingerprint inputs

C1. fingerprint salt missing
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_DEPENDENCY_MISSING (salt must be resolvable; KMS ref or config ref).

C2. fingerprint key_fields includes disallowed fields
- Disallowed: raw prompt text, user_id, customer_id (direct), Authorization header.
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED.
- Allowed: route_id, request_id (if stable), normalized conversation id, hashed tenant id (internal), model family id.

C3. fingerprint uses request_id only (non-stable across retries)
- Expectation: Allow but warn in Console: may increase variance; not stable across client retries.

C4. collision handling
- Expectation: Hash collisions extremely unlikely; runtime should not crash.
- Test: force collision in unit test (mock hash) -> ensure deterministic but safe behavior.

C5. bucketing method unsupported
- Input: bucketing.method="bernoulli_random"
- Expectation: Reject for v1 if only consistent hashing is supported (per ADR).


SECTION D — Budgets, timeouts, and fail-open guarantees

D1. fail_open=false requested
- Input: fail_open=false
- Expectation: Reject or force true.
- Recommendation: Force true at validation (store true) and return a warning field in API response. If warnings not supported, reject.

D2. timeouts.total_ms missing
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID.

D3. timeouts.total_ms > hard max
- Hard max proposal: 200ms (Hosted), 300ms (Dedicated), configurable (Private).
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED or clamp.
- Recommendation: Reject; clamping surprises customers.

D4. connect_ms > total_ms
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID.

D5. max_parallel <= 0
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID.

D6. max_parallel too high
- Input: max_parallel=10_000
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
- Limit proposal: 100 per route per POP/cluster (tune by mode).

D7. max_bytes too high / missing
- Expectation: If missing, default to conservative limit.
- Validate capture body truncation works (see Streaming section too).

D8. Shadow target error storms should trip circuit breaker
- Not strictly config validation, but integration: set reasonable default breaker thresholds.
- Test: target 5xx rate > X% for Y seconds -> mirroring stops, user path unaffected.

D9. Shadow scoring queue backlog should not block routing
- Validate: scoring pipeline lag triggers “shadow_scoring_lagging” alert but no impact to control.


SECTION E — Multi-region routes + cross-region shadowing

E1. Route is multi-region (active-active) and shadow target in same region
- Expectation: Valid. Shadow request should be sent in-region to avoid cross-region egress/latency.

E2. Route is multi-region, shadow target only available in subset of regions
- Expectation: Valid if runtime can select nearest compatible region; else reject.
- Recommendation: For v1, require shadow target “region_policy=follow_control_region”. Reject if not supported.

E3. Explicit cross-region shadowing requested (e.g., control us-east, shadow eu-west)
- Expectation: Reject by default (privacy/egress). Allow only with explicit override + compliance ack.

E4. Dedicated tenant pinned region, but shadow target points to Hosted shared region
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED (data isolation risk).

E5. Private deployment with no multi-region control plane
- Expectation: Validate allowed regions list; reject unknown.


SECTION F — Fallback policies + capacity tiering

F1. Control route has fallback to compatible model variant
- Expectation: Shadow should mirror the *actual resolved control* inputs/metadata, but shadow target selection should remain stable.
- Test: when control falls back, does shadow experiment still label “control_model_resolved_id”? (telemetry requirement).

F2. Shadow target uses fallback policy
- Recommendation: Allowed if it’s part of the target variant; but we must label “shadow_model_resolved_id” too.
- Validation: Ensure telemetry dims include resolved ids; reject if pipeline not ready? (probably allow; operational risk).

F3. Shadow target requires tool/function calling but control doesn’t
- Expectation: Valid; requests mirrored as-is. Shadow output may error; that’s part of evaluation.
- Validation: ensure request type compatibility (see Request types).

F4. Control uses “autoscale burst” tier; shadow should not consume reserved quotas
- Expectation: Shadow traffic should use separate budget bucket.
- Validation: require shadow_quota_class set to “shadow” (not customer-visible).


SECTION G — Request types compatibility

G1. chat.completions request mirrored to embeddings model
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID; target must support same request type.

G2. embeddings request mirrored to rerank target
- Expectation: Reject.

G3. rerank request mirrored to rerank target with different top_k constraints
- Expectation: Allow if target supports; validation checks top_k within allowed range.

G4. structured output / JSON schema mode
- Expectation: Mirror includes json_schema. Target must advertise support.
- Reject if target lacks capability: SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED.

G5. tool calling enabled
- Mirror includes tool definitions + tool_choice.
- Validate max tool count/size budgets; shadow path should enforce same payload size truncation.

G6. long context / large messages
- Validate: if request exceeds shadow max_bytes, shadow request is dropped (counted as “shadow_skipped_payload_too_large”), not erroring control.


SECTION H — Streaming shadowing behavior

H1. streaming=true, mirror_mode=full
- Expectation: Shadow path mirrors the prompt immediately and either:
  (a) requests non-streaming response from shadow target; OR
  (b) requests streaming but captures only first N tokens.
- Validation: Only supported mode must be enforced. If we only support (a) in v1, reject mirror_mode=streaming_capture.

H2. streaming=true, mirror_mode=prompt_only
- Expectation: Shadow target gets same input; response captured asynchronously; control streaming unaffected.
- Validate allowed.

H3. streaming=true with capture_limit_tokens unset
- Expectation: Default to safe value (e.g., 256) to limit cost.
- Validation: if mirror_mode implies capture, require explicit limit OR default.

H4. streaming=false but mirror_mode requires streaming capture
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_INVALID.

H5. Client disconnect mid-stream
- Expectation: Control path may terminate. Shadow path should also terminate quickly; no runaway shadow compute.
- Test: simulate disconnect; ensure shadow cancellation triggers.

H6. stop_conditions invalid
- Input: stop_conditions contains unsupported rule (e.g., “until_tool_call_only”).
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED.

H7. Shadow target streaming chunk parse errors
- Expectation: Shadow output marked error; control unaffected.


SECTION I — Headers, metadata, and privacy controls

I1. headers: allowlist includes Authorization
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED.

I2. headers: allowlist empty + default behavior
- Expectation: Define default: forward minimal required headers only (trace ids, request id, content-type).
- Validation: if missing config, apply default.

I3. metadata passthrough includes customer PII fields
- Example: x-user-email, x-org-name
- Expectation: Reject or force drop.
- Recommendation: Force drop unless explicitly hashed. Reject if config tries to forward.

I4. redact_profile_id missing but mode requires it
- Dedicated/Private with “store prompt for 24h” requires redact_profile_id.
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_DEPENDENCY_MISSING.

I5. retention_profile_id exceeds tenant allowance
- Example: Dedicated tenant contract allows 24h, config requests 30d.
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_RBAC_DENIED or LIMIT_EXCEEDED (need consistent semantics; probably RBAC/entitlement).

I6. opt-out: customer disables prompt retention
- Expectation: Shadow still allowed, but telemetry stores hashes only; sampled examples UI disabled.
- Validation: ensure config does not request example storage.


SECTION J — Cardinality + labeling guardrails (observability)

J1. Policy attempts to emit tags: prompt_id
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED.

J2. Policy uses dynamic label from request header
- Example: label_by="x-user-id"
- Expectation: Reject.

J3. Allowed label set
- route_id, experiment_id, control_model_id, shadow_model_id, region, request_type, rubric_version
- Validation: ensure only allowed keys.

J4. Segment filters in Console
- Even if Console supports filtering by “customer_id”, metrics pipeline must bucket/aggregate safely.
- Validation: any config specifying segment dims must be checked against allowlist.


SECTION K — RBAC, auditability, and lifecycle

K1. Create policy without required permission
- Expectation: Reject SHADOW_POLICY_RBAC_DENIED.
- Tests: viewer role vs editor role; Dedicated customer admin vs regular.

K2. Update policy requires audit log
- Expectation: Always write audit log entry including diff summary.
- Validation: if audit subsystem down, policy write should fail (control plane correctness), but existing policy remains.

K3. Delete policy while experiment running
- Expectation: Allowed; runtime stops mirroring quickly (within cache TTL).
- Validate: deletion is a soft-delete for retention window.

K4. Feature flag gating
- If tenant not enabled for shadow traffic, reject with SHADOW_POLICY_RBAC_DENIED (entitlement).


SECTION L — Private deployments constraints

L1. Private (air-gapped) with no external scoring workers
- Expectation: Shadowing can be enabled but scoring must be “local-only” or disabled.
- Validation: if scoring_mode="redwood_managed" in Private air-gapped, reject SHADOW_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED.

L2. Private storage backend not configured
- Expectation: If prompt/response retention requested but no object store configured, reject DEPENDENCY_MISSING.

L3. SIEM export required
- For regulated tenants, enabling shadow policy must ensure audit logs export is enabled.
- Validation: if compliance_profile requires export, reject if not configured.


SECTION M — Migration / backward compatibility

M1. Policy schema version mismatch
- Input: shadow_policy_version="v0" (old)
- Expectation: Either migrate automatically or reject.
- Recommendation: Support v0->v1 migration for internal dogfood configs; reject for external API.

M2. Default fields introduced in v1.1
- Example: streaming_behavior.capture_limit_tokens becomes required.
- Expectation: Older stored configs should continue to work via defaults.
- Test: load old config; runtime behavior safe.


SECTION N — Concrete “golden configs” for tests

N1. Minimal valid (non-streaming)
- enabled=true
- sampling_rate=0.05
- targets=[{variant_ref=candidate_A}]
- timeouts={connect_ms=20,total_ms=150}
- budgets={max_parallel=20}
- Expectation: Accept.

N2. Valid with 2 targets + deterministic bucketing
- sampling_rate=0.1
- targets=[candidate_A, candidate_B]
- bucketing uses stable fields (route_id + normalized_conversation_id) + salt_ref
- Expectation: Accept.

N3. Valid streaming prompt-only
- streaming_behavior.mirror_mode=prompt_only
- capture_limit_tokens not required (since no capture)
- Expectation: Accept.

N4. Invalid: cross-type
- control request_type=chat
- target request_type=embeddings
- Expectation: Reject.


Open questions (track separately; don’t block writing tests)
- A1 strict vs lenient handling when enabled=false.
- Max targets (4 vs 2) and whether per-target budgets are needed.
- Whether sampling_rate=1 requires additional confirmation/entitlement.
- Whether route+rollout both can specify policy with precedence.

TODO for implementation
- Convert sections A–M into table-driven unit tests in shadow-traffic-policy-service.
- Add integration tests in routing: fail-open, streaming disconnect, circuit breaker trip.
- Align error_code taxonomy with Console API contract draft (Chloe / Dylan).

Changelog
- 2026-02-16: Added streaming edge cases (H5/H6), Dedicated->Hosted isolation check (E4), and RBAC/audit requirements (K2/K4) after SRE review thread + beta oncall prep notes.
